description: Team Astrons is a 6-member team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, We’re building "ExoPath," a game merging live NASA TAP API data with relativistic physics and (Environmental Control and Life Support System) ECLSS systems. I'm Vetri, leading an interdisciplinary crew of engineers and researchers. We’re seeking passionate Frontend UI developers and Backend whizzes to bring our simulation to life. Join us to experience!
summary:
EXOSKY – Discover the Universe Through the Eyes of Other Worlds

EXOSKY is an interactive platform for space exploration aimed at making astronomy and planetary science fun, engaging, and educational. We have created a web application, which enables users to explore planets and exoplanets, examine 3D models of planets, create custom-made space mission with destinations, spacecraft, launch vehicle, satellites, rovers, and instruments.

Our platform offers exoplanet explorer with the NASA Exoplanet Archive database, planet comparison tool, creative constellation creator, and scientific data center with resources of NASA, ESA, and ISRO.

The EXOSKY platform solves the problem of making the process of comprehending complex astronomical data more intuitive with the help of interactive visualizations, real scientific data, and hands-on discovery.

It creates a connection between scientific information and public knowledge and makes space science exciting and educational
details:
EXOSKY – Explore the Universe Through Another World's Eyes

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

EXOSKY is an interactive web-based space exploration platform that makes astronomy and planetary science easier and more engaging to understand. It provides six main features: Mission Builder, Explore Exoplanets, Constellation Creator, Planet Comparison, Scientific Data Centre, and Settings.

Users can select planets such as Earth, Mars, Venus, and Mercury, explore interactive 3D planetary models, and learn about their characteristics. The Mission Builder allows users to create a space mission by choosing destinations, spacecraft, and mission equipment, followed by an interactive mission simulation. The Exoplanet Explorer allows users to browse planets beyond our Solar System, search and filter them, and retrieve confirmed-planet records from the NASA Exoplanet Archive. Users can also create and save custom constellations and compare planetary information.

2. What benefits does it have?

EXOSKY makes complex scientific information easier to understand through interactive visualizations and hands-on learning. It encourages users to explore space independently rather than only reading theoretical information. It brings together planetary exploration, mission planning, exoplanet information, creative activities, and scientific data resources in one platform.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to increase interest in astronomy, space science, and scientific research, especially among students and young learners. We aim to make space exploration more accessible, inspire curiosity about worlds beyond Earth, and encourage the next generation to learn more about science, technology, and space missions.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

We developed EXOSKY as a browser-based application using:

  • HTML5 – application structure.
  • CSS3 and Tailwind CSS – styling, layout, and responsive interface.
  • JavaScript (ES6) – application logic and interactivity.
  • React 18 – reusable components and interface state management.
  • Three.js and WebGL – interactive 3D planetary visualization.
  • GLTFLoader and GLB models – loading 3D planetary assets.
  • HTML Canvas API – interactive constellation creation.
  • NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP API – retrieving confirmed exoplanet records.
  • Web Audio API – optional ambient soundscape.
  • Babel Standalone – browser-side JSX transformation.
  • Lucide Icons – interface icons.
  • Browser Local Storage – saving user selections, settings, and constellation designs.

The project runs in a modern web browser and uses no dedicated hardware requirement beyond a compatible computer or device.

5. How is the project creative?

EXOSKY combines scientific exploration with creativity and interactive simulation. Instead of presenting astronomy as static information, it lets users interact with 3D planets, design their own constellations, compare planetary properties, and build a space mission step by step. The combination of scientific information, visual exploration, mission simulation, and creative activities makes the platform an engaging way to experience space science.

6. What factors did the team consider?

We considered accessibility, ease of use, educational value, scientific reliability, visual clarity, and interactive experience while developing the platform. We also considered browser compatibility, performance, responsive layouts, and the ability to preserve user-created work. Scientific data sources are identified in the Data Centre, and illustrative demo estimates are distinguished from measured planetary conditions so that users are not misled about exoplanet habitability.

EXOSKY's central idea is to transform space science from something people simply read about into something they can explore, understand, and experience interactively.
